result:
I checked all 150 rules in `pricebook.py` against their docstrings and the shared rules in the module docstring. 11 of them didn't match, and I fixed all 11.

| Rule | Docstring says | What the code did | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | whole 15% | discounted only the units above the threshold (marginal) | discount on the whole amount |
| 150 | whole 10% | discounted only the units above the threshold (marginal) | discount on the whole amount |
| 96 | marginal 7% | discounted the whole amount | units above the threshold only |
| 128 | marginal 8% | discounted the whole amount | units above the threshold only |
| 12 | cap 30,000 won | cap applied only when the discount was over 60,000 won | cap always applies |
| 20 | discount capped | the price (`min(base, 30000)`) was capped instead | cap the discount |
| 56 | discount capped | the discounted amount was capped instead | cap the discount |
| 70 | discount capped | the discounted amount was capped instead | cap the discount |
| 107 | 2% | 3% | 2% |
| 120 | 5% | 6% | 5% |
| 136 | 5% | 6% | 5% |

**How I checked:** I wrote a separate script that reads each docstring and computes the correct price from it. It compares that with each function for quantities 0–259 plus a few large values, across a range of unit prices. Thresholds are at most 100, so every boundary is covered. It also checks that negative inputs raise `ValueError`. Before the fix it found the 11 mismatches above; after the fix it finds none. `RULES` and `quote()` still work.

The check script and a copy of the original file are in `/tmp/chk/`.

STATUS: DONE
